findings.issue_text: In addGuests.handler.ts:46-48, the team permission check uses `&&` instead of `||`: the variable is named isTeamAdminOrOwner but the code requires the caller to be both admin and owner. Since a user has one membership role, this either denies team admins who aren't owners or is always false, making the entire team-permission path dead — legitimate team booking managers get FORBIDDEN.

In addGuests.handler.ts:146-153, EventManager is built with the requester's credentials rather than the booking organizer's credentials. booking.references point at the organizer's credentialIds (the query eagerly loads booking.user.credentials but then doesn't use it), so when the caller is an attendee or team admin, their credential list won't contain the referenced credentialIds — the organizer's real calendar event either silently never gets the new guests or the update throws after guests were already written to the DB.

The server-side schema (addGuests.schema.ts:6) lacks the intra-list uniqueness check that the client enforces: ZAddGuestsInputSchema is just z.array(z.string().email()) and the handler's filter (addGuests.handler.ts:71-75) only removes emails already on the booking, never deduplicating within the request. So guests: ["a@x.com", "a@x.com"] passes both filters and hits createMany twice, creating duplicate attendee rows (same for concurrent requests due to check-then-act with no transaction/lock). Client-side validation is not enforcement.

In addGuests.handler.ts:67-74, email comparisons are case-sensitive: the blacklist is lowercased but `guest` is compared as-submitted, so BLOCKED@x.com bypasses blocked@x.com. The same defect exists in the dedup (guest === attendee.email), allowing John@X.com to be added when john@x.com is already an attendee, creating a duplicate person. The abuse-control env var is bypassed by changing one letter's case.

In addGuests.handler.ts:89-99 vs :153, updateCalendarAttendees failure happens after the DB write and is not caught. If it throws (wrong credentials, Google outage, revoked token), the mutation rejects even though the guests were already added — leaving inconsistent state (DB has guests, calendar/emails don't), the dialog shows an error, onSuccess never fires, and retrying with the same emails yields a misleading BAD_REQUEST 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' validation error for a state that is actually 'already added'.
In addGuests.handler.ts:155-159, email failure is swallowed with the error object discarded.

In addGuests.handler.ts:52-56, the isAttendee check grants add-guests rights to any user whose email appears in booking.attendees; since guests added by this endpoint themselves become attendees, any guest can recursively call addGuests to add more guests, who can add more indefinitely — guests who were only ever invited inherit management rights over the booking, while the UI only exposes this action to organizers, showing the API-level breadth is unintended.

The attendee-based authz is trivially reachable for abuse: any authenticated user can become an 'attendee' of any booking simply by booking any public (free) event type, then use addGuests to send branded calendar-invite emails (with meeting details, video call URL/password, and replyTo set to the organizer's address) to arbitrary email addresses of their choosing — a spam/phishing primitive where replies go to the victim organizer.

addGuests.schema.ts:5 defines guests as z.array(z.string().email()) with no .max() bound, and the handler never enforces eventType.guestsLimit or seatsPerTimeSlot (seatsPerTimeSlot is read into evt but never used as a cap); one authorized caller can submit thousands of emails in a single or repeated requests, causing unbounded DB writes, calendar API calls, and outbound email — an email-bombing/DoS amplifier and a capacity bypass for seat-limited event types.
In addGuests.handler.ts:70-78, BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entries are lowercased but the guest email is compared as-is, so case variants like Evil@Example.com sail past a blacklisted evil@example.com.

BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS is split on ',' without trimming, so with the typical config style 'a@x.com, b@y.com' every entry after the first contains a leading space and can never match any validated email, making the blacklist control effectively dead when operators configure it (e.g., to protect internal addresses).

In addGuests.handler.ts:46-48, isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||, requiring the user to be both admin and owner; this fails closed (no bypass) but silently denies legitimate team admins — a broken permission check (the isTeamOwner call is also redundant since owner implies admin in Cal.com's model).

In addGuests.handler.ts, attendees are persisted via createMany (~lines 100-104) before eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking) (line 165), which is not wrapped in try/catch; if the calendar update throws (bad/missing credentials, API error), the client gets a 500 but the guests are already in the DB and no emails were sent, and a retry then hits the uniqueGuests.length === 0 branch (line 80) returning the misleading emails_must_be_unique_valid BAD_REQUEST — leaving the user stuck with guests added, never notified, and the calendar never updated.
The email try/catch at addGuests.handler.ts:167-171 swallows err without logging it.

In addGuests.handler.ts:158-165, calendar sync is built from the requester's credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) + new EventManager({ ...user })) instead of the booking organizer's; when the caller is an attendee or team admin rather than booking.userId, the organizer's calendar credentials are never used, so the organizer's Google/Outlook event attendee list is not updated — despite the booking being fetched with user: { include: { credentials: true } } (lines 35-39), those organizer credentials are never used.

In addGuests.handler.ts:76, guest === attendee.email is a case-sensitive comparison, so Alice@Example.com can be added when alice@example.com already attends the same booking, creating duplicate attendees (and duplicate emails) that differ only in case.

The server-side schema (addGuests.schema.ts) lacks the intra-request uniqueness refinement that the client-side schema in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:20-24 enforces, so exact duplicate emails within one request reach createMany, causing either a DB unique-constraint 500 or duplicate rows depending on constraints.

addGuests.handler.ts:54-56 performs no booking.status check, so guests can be added to CANCELLED/REJECTED bookings; new guests then receive an ICS with status 'CONFIRMED' (attendee-add-guests-email.ts:20) for an event that no longer exists, and calendar updates are attempted against a cancelled event.

addGuests.handler.ts:124-147 builds evt without a team field, but sendAddGuestsEmails (email-manager.ts:529-534) loops over calendarEvent.team?.members to notify fellow team hosts; since team is always undefined, team members silently never receive the 'guests added' email — the team-member notification branch is dead code.

The `guests` input in `addGuests.schema.ts` is unbounded — `z.array(z.string().email())` has no `.max()` length cap — so an attacker-chosen N drives createMany inserts of N attendee rows, a refetch of all attendees, N translation loads, and N+1 concurrent email promises (each with ICS generation + React SSR render) within one synchronous request; since any booking attendee (and every added guest becomes one) is authorized via the `isAttendee` path, any guest can trigger an arbitrarily large write + email fan-out repeatedly, making this a spam/DoS amplification vector (fix: `.max(N)` e.g. 10-25 plus a rate limit on the mutation).

No server-side dedupe within the request: `uniqueGuests` at `addGuests.handler.ts:74-78` only filters against existing attendees and the blacklist, never deduping `guests` against itself, and the server schema lacks the uniqueness refinement that exists only client-side in `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` — so a payload like ["a@x.com","a@x.com"] sent via the API creates two attendee rows, sends duplicate emails, and those duplicates are then included in every future all-attendees email loop for the booking.
The email comparison `guest === attendee.email` at `addGuests.handler.ts:74-78` is case-sensitive, so `A@x.com` and `a@x.com` both get inserted.

Email fan-out runs inline in the mutation with no batching or concurrency cap (`email-manager.ts:529-550` + `addGuests.handler.ts:166-170`): all organizer/team/attendee email promises are created at once and `Promise.all`'d, awaited in the request path with no chunking, queue, or concurrency limit, so request latency, event-loop pressure, and memory (all rendered HTML + ICS strings held simultaneously) scale linearly with total attendee count; should be batched (p-limit or chunks) or pushed to a background job.

O(N×M) membership checks: `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` inside the `attendees.map` at `email-manager.ts:542`, and the same-shaped `guests.filter(... attendees.some(...))` at `addGuests.handler.ts:74-78`, are quadratic string scans — a `Set` should be used instead.

N+1 translation loads at `addGuests.handler.ts:108-120`: a full i18n translator (filesystem read of the locale JSON) is loaded for every attendee, usually the same locale repeatedly; it should be memoized per distinct locale.

Redundant organizer query at `addGuests.handler.ts:58-68`: the initial `findFirst` already includes `user: { include: { destinationCalendar, credentials } }` with all scalar fields, so `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow` re-queries the same user on every call; should use `booking.user`.
In the case where the booking's `userId` is null, `findFirstOrThrow` with `id: 0` at `addGuests.handler.ts:58-68` throws a raw Prisma P2025 error instead of a TRPCError.

Team-permission DB queries at `addGuests.handler.ts:46-48` run before the free checks: `isTeamAdmin` is awaited, then (if true) `isTeamOwner`, before the pure in-memory `isOrganizer`/`isAttendee` checks — wasting 1-2 membership queries in the common organizer/attendee path, and they also fire with `teamId ?? 0` for personal (non-team) bookings; reorder to check organizer/attendee first.

The `&&` between `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner` at `addGuests.handler.ts:47-48` contradicts the variable name `isTeamAdminOrOwner`: only users who are both pass, so plain team admins get FORBIDDEN — it should be `||`.

The team-member email branch at `email-manager.ts:532-538` is dead code: `evt` built at `addGuests.handler.ts:124-146` never sets `team`, so `calendarEvent.team?.members` is always undefined and the branch never executes.

`EventManager` at `addGuests.handler.ts:157-164` is constructed with the caller's credentials (`ctx.user`) instead of the booking organizer's, so a non-organizer attendee adding guests will fail (or no-op) the calendar attendee update.
The blacklist check at `addGuests.handler.ts:77` lowercases the blacklist but not the guest emails, so `User@x.com` bypasses `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`.

`addGuests.handler.ts:167` passes raw `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests` to `sendAddGuestsEmails`, so re-submitting an already-present email sends that attendee the wrong template ('scheduled' instead of 'guests added').

addGuests.handler.ts:46-48 — isTeamAdminOrOwner uses `&&` instead of `||` in the team-permission check, requiring the caller to be both team admin AND owner; this either locks out non-owner team admins or makes the whole team branch dead code, so the intended team-admin authorization path doesn't work.

addGuests.handler.ts:158-165 — EventManager is built from the requester's credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)) instead of the booking organizer's, even though the prisma query fetches booking.user.credentials and never uses it; for non-organizer callers the EventManager credentials don't match the booking's calendar/external-event references, so updateCalendarAttendees silently fails and new guests never appear on the actual calendar event.

addGuests.schema.ts:5-7 + addGuests.handler.ts:74-78 — server input contract is weaker than the client's and duplicates are persisted: the server schema lacks the uniqueness refinement the dialog has, and uniqueGuests only de-dupes against existing attendees (case-sensitively), never within the input array; a direct API call with ['a@x.com', 'a@x.com'] passes validation and createMany inserts duplicate attendee rows (no unique constraint on (bookingId, email)), producing duplicate emails and duplicate ATTENDEE lines in the ICS.

addGuests.handler.ts:70-77 — BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS comparison is case-sensitive on one side: the env list is lowercased but blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) compares the raw, un-lowercased guest input, so submitting Blocked@Example.com bypasses the blacklist; relatedly, when all guests are filtered out as blacklisted the user gets the misleading 'emails must be unique and valid' error.

addGuests.handler.ts (fetch at 26–44, authorization at 54) — no booking.status guard: the mutation adds guests to CANCELLED/REJECTED bookings, so new guests receive an ICS with status CONFIRMED and a scheduled-style email for an event that no longer exists, and updateCalendarAttendees runs against the calendar record of a cancelled event.

addGuests.schema.ts:6 — no .max() (or .min(1)) bound on the guests array: one request can carry thousands of emails, causing thousands of createMany rows and thousands of external emails (with the meeting link) fired from the platform's mailer by any booking attendee; unbounded fan-out on a new external input.

addGuests.handler.ts:124-147 + email-manager.ts:531-537 — evt never sets team, so the team-member notification branch in sendAddGuestsEmails (which iterates calendarEvent.team?.members) is dead code; for team/round-robin/collective bookings no team member is ever notified that guests were added.

addGuests.handler.ts:168 — raw guests is passed to sendAddGuestsEmails instead of uniqueGuests, so email-manager.ts:541's newGuests.includes(attendee.email) matches emails that were filtered out (already attendees / blacklisted); an existing attendee redundantly re-submitted receives a full duplicate AttendeeScheduledEmail ('you're booked') instead of the guests-added notice.

addGuests.handler.ts:58-68 — findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } }) throws an unhandled Prisma error for a booking with a null userId, resulting in a 500 internal error instead of a controlled TRPC error.

AddGuestsDialog.tsx:42-45 — error toast has a dead fallback and leaks raw internals: the template string `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}` is never falsy (worst case 'undefined: undefined'), making the `|| t('unable_to_add_guests')` fallback unreachable, and it surfaces raw TRPC codes and runs t() over non-translation-key messages (e.g., Zod error JSON).

AddGuestsDialog.tsx:35-41, 56 — isInvalidEmail is never reset on success (or reopen): on a successful add the dialog closes and inputs reset but the error flag stays true, so reopening shows 'Emails must be unique and valid' with no invalid input present.

addGuests.handler.ts:167-171 — email failure is swallowed and success is still returned: catch (err) logs a static string via console.log (the error object is discarded) and the mutation returns { message: 'Guests added' } regardless, making failures undiagnosable in production and misreported to the caller.

addGuests.handler.ts:145 — no seat-capacity check for seat-based event types: seatsPerTimeSlot is passed through to the ICS/event payload but nothing verifies attendees + guests ≤ seatsPerTimeSlot, so guests can overbook seated events and corrupt seat accounting.
addGuests.handler.ts:83-90 — guests are created with name: '' — blank names flow into the attendee list UI and email headers (to: ' <email>', 'Hello ,') for every downstream email.

Non-atomic mutation in addGuests.handler.ts: guests are committed to the DB via prisma.booking.update before the calendar sync, with no try/catch or inspection of results around eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees; if the calendar call throws, guests are already persisted, and the user's retry fails with the misleading 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' error because the dedup filter empties uniqueGuests — leaving DB state with guests added but no emails sent and no calendar update

EventManager is constructed from the requester's credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)) instead of the booking organizer's, so for authorized attendees and team admins/owners on team bookings the calendar reference credentialId won't match and updateCalendarAttendees silently no-ops or throws — guests are added and emails sent but the external Google/Outlook event is never updated with no error surfaced; should use booking.user
isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...) instead of ||, contradicting its name, so a team admin who is not the team owner is denied with an opaque FORBIDDEN error

Email-send failures are swallowed: catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); } never logs err and uses console.log instead of console.error/logger, so guests are added but receive no notification, the caller has no way to know, and the failure is undiagnosable with no retry or error detail captured

Server ZAddGuestsInputSchema lacks the unique-email refinement the client enforces, and the handler's dedup only filters against existing attendees rather than duplicates within the request — a payload like ["a@x.com","a@x.com"] reaches createMany, causing a raw Prisma unique-constraint 500 or duplicate attendee rows plus duplicate emails/ICS invites

Case-sensitivity asymmetry defeats the blacklist and dedup checks: blacklist entries are lowercased but guest emails are compared as-typed with exact-match includes and ===, so "Admin@Example.com" bypasses a blacklisted "admin@example.com" and case-variants of existing attendees create near-duplicate guests; the client's Set-based uniqueness is also case-sensitive and won't catch this

No booking status check: the query and authorization never check booking.status or that the booking is in the future, so guests can be added to cancelled or past bookings, sending status CONFIRMED REQUEST ICS files for an event whose calendar entry was deleted and targeting a deleted external event with updateCalendarAttendees

TOCTOU between the dedup read and the write: authorization and duplicate filtering happen on the findFirst snapshot with several awaits before createMany commits, so two concurrent requests adding the same guest both pass the filter and both write — producing duplicate attendees or a raw unique-constraint 500; read+write should be wrapped in a transaction or P2002 caught with a clean error

Unbounded guests array: addGuests.schema.ts has no .max() and no rate limit anywhere in the chain, so an authorized user (including any booking attendee) can submit thousands of emails in one mutation, triggering createMany, an inline mass email fan-out, and a calendar update with all attendees — a request-timeout/mail-bombing/DB-bloat vector

Dead error fallback in the error toast: `"${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}"` is always a truthy string, so `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` never falls back — when code/message are missing the user sees "undefined: undefined" and the intended fallback string is unreachable

isInvalidEmail is never reset on success or when the dialog closes via onOpenChange — only the Cancel button clears it — so after a validation failure followed by a successful add (or closing via ESC/overlay/X), the warning is still true and reappears immediately on the next open over empty inputs

Raw guests input (not the filtered uniqueGuests) is passed to sendAddGuestsEmails, so if the request includes an email that already belongs to an attendee, newGuests.includes(attendee.email) matches that existing attendee and they are sent a duplicate full AttendeeScheduledEmail ("you're booked") instead of the intended "guests added" notice

In addGuests.handler.ts:46-48, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `&&` (isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)) where the intent — and the variable name — requires `||`; since owners are a subset of admins in the role model, the gate collapses to owner-only and non-owner team admins get FORBIDDEN on a normal, intended flow.
In addGuests.handler.ts, both the admin and owner queries run even when `eventType?.teamId` is undefined (`?? 0`), so non-team bookings pay two pointless DB round-trips.

addGuests.handler.ts:168 passes the raw `guests` array to `sendAddGuestsEmails` instead of the filtered `uniqueGuests` used for the DB write (line 74), so an existing attendee who was merely re-typed in the dialog gets a full scheduled-confirmation email resent.

Case-asymmetric blacklist comparison in addGuests.handler.ts:70-78: `blacklistedGuestEmails` entries are `.toLowerCase()`d (line 71) but `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` (line 77) compares against the raw guest, so `Spam@x.com` bypasses a blacklisted `spam@x.com`.
Case-sensitive comparison `guest === attendee.email` at addGuests.handler.ts:76 allows a case-variant of an existing attendee to create a duplicate attendee record (and then misrouted emails).

AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-29 redefines `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` — the same exported name as the server's schema in addGuests.schema.ts but a different shape (bare array vs `{bookingId, guests}`) — creating two sources of truth with different semantics for a valid guests list; it also re-instantiates the schema on every render instead of being hoisted and reused from addGuests.schema.ts.

Uniqueness is enforced only by the client-side refine: the server schema (addGuests.schema.ts:6) and the handler's `uniqueGuests` filter never dedupe within a single request, so a direct API call with `["a@x.com","a@x.com"]` either inserts duplicate attendee rows or trips the `(bookingId, email)` constraint.

Organizer/actor confusion in addGuests.handler.ts:35-40 and 158-163: the booking query eagerly includes the organizer's credentials (`user: { include: { credentials: true } }`) but they are never used, while `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` builds the EventManager from the caller — who may be a mere attendee or a team admin with no connected calendar — so `updateCalendarAttendees` on the organizer's calendar depends on the wrong actor's credentials (silent no-op or throw after the DB write).

addGuests.handler.ts:167-171 swallows email failure: `catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails") }` discards `err`, logs at info level, and the handler still returns success, leaving nothing to debug when email delivery breaks; minimum fix is `console.error(err)`.

AddGuestsDialog.tsx:32-33, 36-41 dialog state isn't tied to open/close: the component stays mounted in BookingListItem so useState persists across open cycles; only Cancel resets `multiEmailValue`/`isInvalidEmail`, Esc/backdrop close (`onOpenChange`) resets nothing, and the success path resets emails but never clears `isInvalidEmail` — leaving a stale 'Emails must be unique and valid' banner over an empty form after reopen.

Dead fallback in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:43-44: `message` is a template literal and therefore always truthy (worst case rendering 'undefined: undefined'), so `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), ...)` can never reach the fallback — the new locale key `unable_to_add_guests` is effectively dead.

sendAddGuestsEmails in email-manager.ts:525-546 clones the sendLocationChangeEmails fan-out skeleton (formatCalEvent → organizer push → team-member loop → attendee map → Promise.all), differing only in the attendee branch; this second copy of the pattern should be extracted into a shared fan-out helper taking per-recipient email factories.

MultiEmail.tsx:46 hardcodes the English `Tooltip content="Remove email"`, shipping untranslated text to every locale and burying a translatable string inside the shared packages/ui package, while the adjacent button uses `t("add_another")`.
Verify that `add_another` exists in common.json: this PR adds `add_emails` but not `add_another`, and if the key is missing the adjacent button renders the raw key.

Speculative `readOnly` path in MultiEmail.tsx (lines 6, 57, 77): the only caller (AddGuestsDialog.tsx:72) passes `readOnly={false}`, so the entire disabled-rendering branch is unexercised generality — drop `readOnly` or wait for a real caller.
MultiEmail.tsx duplicates the 'append empty email' button logic verbatim in two branches (lines 64-68 and 83-87); the two buttons should be unified.

MultiEmailLazy.tsx:4 is a copied lazy-load wrapper with a false justification: the 'these are like 40kb' comment is copy-pasted from PhoneInputLazy/AddressInputLazy which lazy-load heavy third-party deps, but MultiEmail has no such dependency — the dynamic wrapper adds an extra chunk and loading indirection for nothing and the comment misleads the next maintainer; export the component directly.
Misleading naming in addGuests.handler.ts:92: `bookingAttendees` holds the updated booking rather than attendees, so `bookingAttendees.attendees` reads like a double-nesting error.

The menu item id and `data-testid` in BookingListItem.tsx:193-197 / AddGuestsDialog are `add_members` for a guests feature, but 'members' already means team members in cal.com — the id actively misleads anyone writing tests or grepping the codebase.

Fat handler with duplicated CalendarEvent assembly in addGuests.handler.ts:124-147: the ~70-line booking→CalendarEvent construction (attendeesList with per-locale translations, videoCallReference extraction, destinationCalendar fallback chain) is hand-rolled inline and mirrors logic in sibling booking handlers — a prime extraction candidate into a shared builder.

The handler's side effects aren't atomic: DB write → external calendar update (which can throw after persistence, leaving guests saved with an error returned to the client) → swallowed emails; separating an `addGuestsToBooking` service from the tRPC handler would make the sequencing and failure modes explicit.

Calendar sync in addGuests.handler.ts:157-165 is built from the caller's credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)) instead of the booking organizer's, while evt.organizer and evt.destinationCalendar point at booking.user — updateCalendarAttendees finds no credential matching the organizer's destination calendar and silently skips, so new guests are never added to the external calendar event even though the mutation returns 'Guests added' success; the include at lines 35-40 fetches booking.user.credentials that are never used, evidence of the mix-up.

Partial-failure ordering in addGuests.handler.ts: attendee rows are persisted to the DB (lines 92-106) before the unguarded calendar call at line 165 (no try/catch, unlike the email send at 167-171); any calendar error (expired token, deleted remote event, API quota) surfaces after the DB write with no rollback, and retrying hits the emails_must_be_unique_valid BAD_REQUEST, leaving guests in the DB with no invite and the user unable to reach a consistent state.

addGuests.handler.ts:46-48 uses && instead of || in the team permission check — isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...) requires the user to be both, so non-owner team ADMINs are wrongly denied the ability to add guests to their team's bookings.

Case-sensitive email comparisons in addGuests.handler.ts:70-77 defeat both the blacklist and the duplicate guard: blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) compares the raw guest string against lowercased blacklist entries so Blacklisted@Example.com bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS and gets stored and emailed, and the exact compare guest === attendee.email lets Bob@x.com duplicate an existing bob@x.com attendee; emails must be lowercased on both sides before comparison.

No server-side uniqueness within a single request and a non-atomic TOCTOU race: addGuests.schema.ts:4-7 has the .refine uniqueness check only in the client dialog, and the handler (lines 74-81) filters only against pre-existing attendees — a direct tRPC call with duplicate emails passes validation and createMany inserts two rows for the same email, and concurrent requests can both pass the 'not already an attendee' filter before either writes, causing duplicate attendee records and double emails/ICS attachments.

Raw guests (not uniqueGuests) is passed to sendAddGuestsEmails at addGuests.handler.ts:168, so in email-manager.ts:537-543 newGuests.includes(attendee.email) matches attendees the handler silently filtered out at lines 74-78 (already on the booking) — those existing attendees receive a full AttendeeScheduledEmail ('your event has been scheduled' + full ICS) instead of the 'new guests added' delta notice.

The team-member notification branch is unreachable dead code: addGuests.handler.ts:124-147 never sets team on the evt object, so the if (calendarEvent.team?.members) guard in email-manager.ts:528-535 can never be true (formatCalEvent is a synchronous formatter that cannot fetch members), and teammate organizers of round-robin/collective bookings are silently never notified that guests were added.

No booking.status or start-time check in addGuests.handler.ts:44-56 — authorization is identity-only, so guests can be added to cancelled/rejected/pending/past bookings; adding guests to a CANCELLED booking sends each new guest an ICS with status CONFIRMED and method REQUEST, resurrecting the cancelled meeting in guests' calendars.

Unbounded guest array plus attendee-permission cascade is an email-amplification abuse vector: addGuests.schema.ts:5-6 has no .max() on guests, and addGuests.handler.ts:52-56 grants add-guests rights to any attendee (including previously added guests), so one operation emails every attendee with meeting credentials, a single user can submit thousands of emails per request, and each added guest can recursively add more.

In AddGuestsDialog.tsx:31-51, the isInvalidEmail validation-error banner is set on failed validation but only reset on Cancel — it still shows after a successful add or dialog reopen (the component stays mounted in BookingListItem.tsx so state persists), and handleAdd (lines 42-44) returns silently with no feedback when all rows are removed and Add is clicked on empty input.

Email-send failures are swallowed with the error object discarded in addGuests.handler.ts:167-170 — catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); } never logs err, making the most likely failure mode (SMTP/render errors) completely undiagnosable while guests appear added and the user sees 'Guests added' success.

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.
